chapters.title: The Place Where Nothing Was Made
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 21

1I went on as far as the place where nothing was made.

2There I saw a terrible thing: no heaven above, and no earth founded beneath — but an unformed and terrible place.

3There I saw seven of the stars of heaven, bound and cast into it together, like great mountains and burning with fire.

4Then I said, "For what sin are they bound, and for what reason have they been cast here?"

5Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me and led me, and he said, "Enoch, why do you ask, and why are you eager for the truth, and why do you search?"

6"These are the angels who transgressed the command of the Lord Most High, and they are bound here until ten thousand ages are completed — the number of the days of their sin."

7From there I went to another place, more terrible than this. I saw a terrible thing: a great fire there, burning and blazing, and the place had a cleft reaching down to the abyss, full of great pillars of fire falling. Neither its extent nor its size could I see, nor could I guess at it.

8Then I said, "How terrible this place is, and how painful to look at!"

9Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said, "Enoch, why are you so afraid and trembling?" I answered, "Because of this terrible place, and because of the sight of this suffering."

10He said to me, "This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be held forever."

Notes

  • The chapter repeats chapter 18. Verses 1–6 describe the same desolate place and the same seven bound stars as 18:12–16, and vv7–10 revisit the chasm of 18:11. The book tours the same two sites twice, with the same angel explaining them. Whether that is a deliberate second pass or two versions of one journey preserved side by side, the doubling is in every witness.

  • v1 "the place where nothing was made" — the Greek word is ἀκατασκεύαστος, akataskeuastos, unbuilt, not constructed. And that is the Septuagint's word for the state of the earth in Genesis 1:2: the earth was invisible and unformed, rendering Hebrew tohu. The prison at the end of the world is described with the vocabulary of the world before creation — a patch that the six days never reached.

  • v2 "no heaven above, and no earth founded beneath" — the same verse says it plainly. Genesis 1 separates the waters and founds the earth; this place has had neither done to it.

  • v5 "why do you ask... why do you search?" — the angel's reply to a perfectly reasonable question is to ask why the question was asked. He answers it anyway in the next verse. It is the only place in the journey where curiosity is treated as something to be remarked on.

  • v6 "These are the angels" — the EOTC Ge'ez, ʾəllu ʾəmuntu malāʾəkt. Knibb's Ge'ez and the Greek read these are among the stars of heaven. The chapter itself has just called them seven stars of heaven (v3), and so does 18:13–15. The EOTC says outright what the book implies throughout: the bound stars are angels. In the dream-vision of chapters 86–88 the Watchers fall from heaven as stars, and at 90:24 the judgment was held first over the stars. The Revelation to John makes the same identification in one sentence: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches (Revelation 1:20).

  • v6 "ten thousand ages" — the Ge'ez. The Greek has ten thousand years, matching what it said at 18:16. The Ge'ez at 18:16 said the year of mystery. Across two tellings of one sentence the two traditions give three different spans.

  • v10 "the prison of the angels" — two prisons for two offenses. The first holds the stars that did not come out at their appointed times (18:15); this one holds the Watchers who went down to women (chapters 6–10). The EOTC calls the prisoners of both places angels (v6, v10). Both are held in the unmade part of the world.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 21
I went on as far as the place where nothing was made.
There I saw a terrible thing: no heaven above, and no earth founded beneath — but an unformed and terrible place.
There I saw seven of the stars of heaven, bound and cast into it together, like great mountains and burning with fire.
Then I said, "For what sin are they bound, and for what reason have they been cast here?"
Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me and led me, and he said, "Enoch, why do you ask, and why are you eager for the truth, and why do you search?"
"These are the angels who transgressed the command of the Lord Most High, and they are bound here until ten thousand ages are completed — the number of the days of their sin."

From there I went to another place, more terrible than this. I saw a terrible thing: a great fire there, burning and blazing, and the place had a cleft reaching down to the abyss, full of great pillars of fire falling. Neither its extent nor its size could I see, nor could I guess at it.
Then I said, "How terrible this place is, and how painful to look at!"

Then Uriel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said, "Enoch, why are you so afraid and trembling?" I answered, "Because of this terrible place, and because of the sight of this suffering."
He said to me, "This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be held forever."

chapters.title: The Four Hollows of the Dead
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 22

1From there I went to another place, and he showed me in the west a great and high mountain of hard rock.

2There were four hollow places in it, deep and wide and very smooth — three of them dark and one bright, and a spring of water in the middle of it. I said, "How smooth these hollows are, and how deep and dark to look at."

3Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said to me, "These hollow places are for the spirits of the souls of the dead to be gathered into. For this they were made, that all the souls of the sons of men should be gathered here.

4These places were made to hold them until the day of their judgment, and until their appointed time — and the appointed time is long, until the great judgment comes upon them."

5I saw the spirits of the sons of men who were dead, and their voice went out as far as heaven and cried out.

6Then I asked Raphael, the angel who was with me, "Whose spirit is this, whose voice goes out like this and cries out as far as heaven?"

7He answered me, "This is the spirit that came out from Abel, whom Cain his brother killed. He brings his case against him until his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is wiped out from among the seed of men."

Why Are They Separated?

8Then I asked about all the hollow places, "Why is one separated from another?"

9He answered me, "These three were made so that the spirits of the dead might be separated. In this way the spirits of the righteous are set apart — this is where the spring of bright water is.

10In this way it was made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth, and judgment was not carried out on them in their lifetime.

11Here their spirits are set apart, in this great pain, until the great day of judgment — of scourges and torments of the accursed, forever. There is the repayment of their spirits, and there He will bind them forever.

12In this way it was set apart for the spirits of those who bring their case, who make it known that they were destroyed, when they were killed in the days of the sinners.

13In this way it was made for the spirits of men who will not be righteous but sinners, complete in transgression, and they will be partners with the lawless. But their spirits will not be killed on the day of judgment, nor will they be raised from here."

14Then I blessed the Lord of glory and said, "Blessed are You, Lord of glory and righteousness, who rule over all forever."

Notes

  • This is the oldest description of the afterlife having rooms. The Hebrew Bible has Sheol, and Sheol is one place where everyone goes. Here the dead are sorted on arrival, held in separate compartments, and the sorting happens before the judgment rather than after it. Everything later literature assumes about a waiting-place with divisions starts in this chapter.

  • v2 "four hollow places... three of them dark and one bright" — and this is where the Greek earns its keep. The Ge'ez says only that there were four beautiful hollow places, deep and dark. The Greek adds the detail that makes the chapter work: three dark, one bright, with a spring in it. Without that line, v9's these three were made contradicts the four of v2. With it, the arithmetic is plain: three compartments for the dead who are being held, and one lit chamber with water for the righteous.

  • v5 "their voice went out as far as heaven and cried out" — the dead are not silent and they are not asleep. What they do in the waiting place is make noise, and the noise reaches heaven.

  • v7 "the spirit that came out from Abel" — Genesis 4:10: the voice of your brother's bloods is crying out to Me from the ground. Genesis has the blood crying once, at the moment of the murder. This book has Abel still crying, thousands of years later, in a room in a mountain, and says he will not stop until Cain's line is extinct. It takes one verse of Genesis and makes it a permanent condition.

  • v7 "he brings his case against him" — the legal vocabulary again, as in chapters 7 and 9. The earth brought a case; Abel is bringing one. In this book the dead have standing.

  • v9 "the spring of bright water" — the one furnished detail in any of the four rooms. Light and water for the righteous; the rest are described only by what happens in them.

  • v13 "their spirits will not be killed on the day of judgment, nor will they be raised from here" — the hardest sentence in the chapter, and the two witnesses differ on the reason. The Greek supplies one the Ge'ez lacks: because those who were afflicted here are punished less than they. Either way the fate described is neither destruction nor resurrection. It is being left where they are, permanently, and the book offers it as a third outcome.

  • v14 "Then I blessed the Lord" — he has just been shown the sorting of every human being who has ever died, including a murdered man still shouting. His response is a blessing. The book does not explain that either.

chapters.title: The Fire That Never Rests
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 23

1From there I went to another place, toward the west, to the ends of the earth.

2I saw a burning fire that ran without resting, and did not stop from its course day or night, but kept going, always the same.

3I asked, "What is this that has no rest?"

4Then Raguel answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said, "This course of fire that you saw, running toward the west, is the fire that pursues all the luminaries of heaven."

Notes

  • v4 "the fire that pursues all the luminaries" — that is the Greek. The Ge'ez says instead that the fire is all the luminaries of heaven. One witness has a fire chasing the lights across the sky; the other has the fire and the lights being the same thing. It is a four-word clause and the two readings describe different machinery.

  • v2 "ran without resting... day or night" — the chapter's whole subject is a thing that never stops. Set against chapter 18, where seven stars were imprisoned for being late, the book's admiration here is for something that keeps perfect time.

  • v1 "toward the west, to the ends of the earth" — west is where this book puts the end of things: the fire of the west (17:4), the river of fire running west (17:5), the mountain of the dead in the west (22:1), and now this. The sun sets there, and the geography follows the sun.

  • On the shortest chapter of the journey — four verses, one question, one answer. The pattern of the whole tour in miniature: he arrives, he sees, he asks, an angel with a name explains. Chapters 17 through 36 are built out of this unit.

chapters.title: The Tree with No Name
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 24

1From there I went to another place of the earth, and he showed me a mountain of fire that burned day and night.

2I went toward it and saw seven magnificent mountains, each different from the others, with precious and beautiful stones, all of them splendid and glorious in appearance and beautiful in form — three toward the east, set one upon another, and three toward the south, one upon another, and deep and rugged ravines, none of them running into another.

3The seventh mountain was in the middle of these, and it rose above them, like the seat of a throne, and fragrant trees surrounded it.

4Among them was a tree such as I had never smelled — no other among them or any other tree was like it. It had a fragrance beyond all spices, and its leaves and its blossom and its wood never wither, forever. Its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit is like the clusters of a date palm.

5Then I said, "Look at this beautiful tree — beautiful to look at, and lovely are its leaves, and its fruit is a delight to the eye."

6Then Michael answered me, one of the holy and honored angels who was with me, and who was set over them.

Notes

  • v2 "three toward the east... three toward the south" — that is the Greek. The Ge'ez has three toward the north. A compass point, and the two witnesses disagree. The same seven mountains appeared back at 18:6, where both witnesses said south — so here the Ge'ez has drifted from its own earlier reading.

  • vv2–3 the seventh in the middle — six mountains in two rows of three, and a seventh standing higher between them. That is the shape of a menorah: three branches, three branches, and a central shaft. The text does not say so; it just gives the arrangement and then compares the middle one to a throne.

  • v4 "a tree such as I had never smelled" — the first thing said about it is its smell, and the second is that nothing is like it. The book is describing the tree of life and will not name it; that comes in the next chapter. Here it is only a tree nobody may touch, which is what it was in Genesis 3:22.

  • v4 "its leaves and its blossom and its wood never wither" — every part of it is permanent. The one thing about it that changes is the fruit, and the fruit is the only part of it anyone will ever be given.

  • v4 "like the clusters of a date palm" — the one ordinary comparison in the description. After beyond all spices and never wither, the fruit is said to look like dates. The book reaches for something a reader has actually eaten.

  • v6 "Michael... who was set over them" — each place on this journey has its own angelic guide: Uriel for the stars and the prison (21:5), Raphael for the dead (22:3), Raguel for the fire (23:4), and now Michael, who ranks above the others, for the tree. The book assigns its most senior angel to the one thing it will not describe plainly.

chapters.title: No Flesh May Touch It
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 25

1He said to me, "Enoch, why do you ask me about the fragrance of this tree, and why do you want to know the truth?"

2Then I answered him, "I want to know about everything, but especially about this tree."

3He answered me, "This high mountain you saw, whose summit is like the throne of God, is His throne, where the Holy and Great One, the Lord of glory, the Eternal King, will sit when He comes down to visit the earth in goodness.

4As for this fragrant tree, no flesh has authority to touch it until the great judgment, when He takes vengeance on all and brings everything to its end forever. Then it will be given to the righteous and the holy.

5Its fruit will be life for the chosen. It will be transplanted toward the north, into the holy place, beside the house of God, the Eternal King.

6Then they will rejoice greatly and be glad, and they will go into the holy place. Its fragrance will be in their bones, and they will live a longer life on earth than your fathers lived, and in their days no torment or plague or affliction will touch them."

7Then I blessed the God of glory, the Eternal King, who has prepared such things for righteous men, and created them, and promised to give them.

Notes

  • v3 the mountain is the throne — chapter 24 said the seventh mountain was like the seat of a throne. Here the comparison is dropped: it is His throne, and the answer to a question about a tree turns out to be about the mountain it stands on.

  • v4 "no flesh has authority to touch it" — Genesis 3:22–24 ends with the man put out of the garden lest he put out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever, with cherubim set to guard the way. This book picks the tree up again at the other end of history: still untouchable, still guarded, but now with a date on it.

  • v4 "then it will be given to the righteous" — the difference between this and Genesis is one word: until. Genesis bars the tree; this bars it until the great judgment. The prohibition becomes a delay.

  • v5 "it will be transplanted... beside the house of God" — the tree does not stay on its mountain. It is moved, and the place it is moved to is the temple. What was lost from a garden comes back into a building.

  • v6 "rejoice greatly" — the source doubles the verb with its own noun, rejoice with rejoicing, the intensifier Hebrew and Ge'ez both use and English does not. It is the same construction as dying you shall die at Genesis 2:17. What it marks is force, not repetition.

  • v6 "its fragrance will be in their bones" — the strangest promise in the chapter and the most physical. Not eaten, not worn: in the bones. The whole description of the tree began with its smell (24:4) and ends with the smell inside the people.

  • v6 "a longer life than your fathers lived" — Enoch's fathers are the men of Genesis 5, who lived eight and nine hundred years. The promise is not immortality; it is more than nine hundred years, which is a strange and very concrete thing to promise.

  • v3 what the Greek and the Ge'ez each say — the Greek has the Eternal King sitting on the throne when he comes down to visit the earth in goodness. The Ge'ez is broken at the same point and repeats itself. Where a sentence is damaged in one witness and clean in the other, this rendering follows the clean one.

chapters.title: The Middle of the Earth
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 26

1From there I went to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed and watered place, where there were branches still sprouting from a tree that had been cut down.

2There I saw a holy mountain, and beneath the mountain, water on the east, and its flow ran toward the south.

3I saw toward the east another mountain higher than this one, and between them a deep ravine with no breadth, and through it water ran beneath the mountain.

4Toward the west of this was another mountain, lower than it and without height, and a deep and dry ravine between them, and another deep and dry ravine at the ends of the three of them.

5All of them had deep ravines of hard rock, and no tree was planted on them.

6I marveled at the rock, and I marveled at the ravine — I marveled greatly.

Notes

  • v1 "the middle of the earth" — and what he describes from here to the end of chapter 27 is Jerusalem, without naming it. A holy mountain, a spring on its east side, a deep ravine on one side and another on the west, meeting at the corner of three. That is the city's actual geography: Mount Zion, the Gihon spring, the Kidron valley east, the Hinnom valley west and south, joining below.

  • v1 "branches still sprouting from a tree that had been cut down" — the Ge'ez; the Greek has only a blessed place with cuttings. The image the Ethiopic preserves is the one Isaiah 11:1 uses for the line of David: a shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch will grow from his roots. A felled tree that is still putting out shoots is how the Hebrew Bible pictures a cut-down dynasty that is not finished.

  • v2 the water runs south — the Greek. The Ge'ez says north. The Gihon runs south, down the Kidron; but the book has already used north for the direction of the holy place in 25:5, so both readings have a pull on them.

  • v5 "no tree was planted on them" — the Greek. The Ge'ez says the opposite: trees were planted upon them. This is the third place in the book where the two witnesses differ by a negative, after 15:11 and 15:12. Here the context decides it: chapter 27 opens by contrasting a land full of trees with the cursed valley between, which only works if the ravines are bare.

  • v6 "I marveled greatly" — he has been shown the throne of God, the tree of life and the storehouses of the winds without comment. What stops him is a rock formation.

chapters.title: The Accursed Valley
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 27

1Then I said, "Why is this land blessed and all full of trees, but this ravine between them accursed?"

2Then Raphael answered me, one of the holy angels who was with me, "This accursed valley is for those who are accursed forever. Here will be gathered all who speak with their mouth an improper word against the Lord, and say hard things about His glory. Here they will be gathered, and here will be their place.

3In the last times, in the days of the true judgment, in the presence of the righteous forever — here the godless will bless the Lord of glory, the Eternal King.

4In the days of their judgment they will bless Him for the mercy He has allotted them."

5Then I blessed the Lord of glory, and I proclaimed His glory and praised Him greatly.

Notes

  • The valley is Gehenna, and this is where it becomes that. The ravine west and south of Jerusalem is the Valley of Hinnom, gei ben Hinnom. It appears twelve times in the Hebrew Bible, and what happens there is child sacrifice: Ahaz burned his sons in the fire there (2 Chronicles 28:3), Manasseh did the same (33:6), and Josiah defiled the Topheth which is in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, so that no one might make his son or daughter pass through the fire (2 Kings 23:10). Nowhere in the Hebrew Bible is it a place of judgment after death. It is a real valley with a real history.

  • And in the Gospels it is the fire of judgment. Greek transliterates gei Hinnom as γέεννα, geenna — the word in Matthew, Mark and Luke that English Bibles print as hell. Between the Hebrew Bible and the New Testament, a rubbish-strewn valley with a memory of burning children became the name of the place where judgment falls. This chapter is that turn, in writing. A book Jude quotes puts the gathering of the accursed in exactly that ravine.

  • v2 "who speak with their mouth an improper word against the Lord" — the offense named is speech. Not idolatry and not murder: hard words about His glory. It is the same charge laid against the wicked in 5:4 — you have spoken great and hard words with your unclean mouth against His greatness — and the book is consistent about what it thinks the worst sin is.

  • v3 "here the godless will bless the Lord" — that is the Greek. The Ge'ez says here the merciful will bless the Lord. It is the difference between the damned being made to praise God and the righteous praising Him over them, and the two witnesses land on opposite parties. The Greek is the harder reading and the one this rendering follows; v4, where they bless Him for mercy allotted to them, reads more naturally of the condemned.

  • v1 the question is about landscape — Enoch does not ask why people are punished. He asks why one valley is cursed when the land around it is full of trees. The book's answers keep arriving as geography.

chapters.title: Toward the East
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 28

1From there I went toward the east, into the middle of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness, alone and empty, yet full of trees.

2They were from this seed, and water gushed out over it from above, and a torrent appeared, running abundantly toward the north-west, and from every side water and dew rose up.

Notes

  • The verses — the EOTC Ge'ez divides this chapter into two verses. Knibb's Ge'ez, the Greek and Charles's English divide the same words into three, and other English editions number it 28:1–3.

  • v1 "the mountain range of the desert" — the Ge'ez. The Greek gives a place name instead: Mandobara, which is not known from anywhere else and which the Ethiopic does not have. It may be a name the Greek preserved and the Ge'ez turned into a description, or a description the Greek misread as a name.

  • v1 "a wilderness, alone and empty, yet full of trees" — the verse sets the two against each other on purpose. The word for the place is desert; what is actually in it is water and growth. The journey east is beginning to arrive somewhere, and chapters 29 to 32 will keep describing fragrant trees until they reach the garden of righteousness.

  • v2 "from this seed" — this seed, as though the reader has already been shown it. Nothing in the preceding chapters identifies it. Both witnesses have the phrase and neither explains it.

From there I went toward the east, into the middle of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness, alone and empty, yet full of trees.
They were from this seed, and water gushed out over it from above, and a torrent appeared, running abundantly toward the north-west, and from every side water and dew rose up.

chapters.title: Trees of Judgment
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 29

1From there I went to another place, beyond the desert, and drew near to the east of that mountain.

2There I saw trees of judgment, giving off a strong fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees were not like one another.

Notes

  • v1 "beyond the desert" — the Ge'ez, emna madbara, where madbar is the word for desert. The Greek again has a place name, Babdera, as it had Mandobara at 28:1. The two names in the Greek and the one word in the Ge'ez look like the same thing seen two ways: a place called by a name, or a name taken as a description.

  • v2 "trees of judgment" — both witnesses have it: Ge'ez ʿəḍawa kʷənnane, Greek dendra kriseōs. Neither explains why fragrant trees would be called trees of judgment. At 25:4 the fragrant tree on the mountain may not be touched until the great judgment, and these trees stand on the road east to the garden (32:3). What the phrase means is not stated anywhere in the book.

  • v2 "the trees were not like one another" — the Ge'ez. The Greek says the opposite kind of thing: their trees were like nut trees. The Ge'ez ʾiyətmāsalu, they did not resemble, and the Greek comparison cannot both stand, and nothing in the chapter decides between them.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 29
From there I went to another place, beyond the desert, and drew near to the east of that mountain.
There I saw trees of judgment, giving off a strong fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees were not like one another.

chapters.title: Cinnamon in the Ravines
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 30

1Beyond it, above these, above the mountain of the east, and not far off, I saw another place, ravines of water that never runs dry.

2I saw a beautiful tree, and its fragrance was like mastic.

3Along the sides of these ravines I saw fragrant cinnamon. Beyond them I went on toward the east.

Notes

  • v1 "not far off" — the Ge'ez. The Greek says the reverse: I went far toward the east. The Ge'ez wa-ʾakko rəḥuq, and not far, and the Greek makran, far, cannot both be right, and nothing else in the chapter decides between them.

  • v1 "water that never runs dry" — the Ge'ez adds that the ravines are like water that does not fail. The Greek has only a ravine of water. After the desert of chapters 28 and 29, the road east is now running with water.

  • v2 "mastic" — Greek schinos, the mastic tree, whose resin was prized for its scent; the Ge'ez word, sakinon, is borrowed from the same Greek. Chapters 29 to 32 name spice after spice: frankincense, myrrh, mastic, cinnamon, galbanum, nard, pepper. The route to the garden of righteousness (32:3) is laid out as a road of incense.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 30
Beyond it, above these, above the mountain of the east, and not far off, I saw another place, ravines of water that never runs dry.
I saw a beautiful tree, and its fragrance was like mastic.
Along the sides of these ravines I saw fragrant cinnamon. Beyond them I went on toward the east.

chapters.title: Nectar and Almond Bark
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 31

1I saw another mountain with trees on it, and water flowed out, and from it came something like nectar, whose name is sarara and galbanum.

2Beyond that mountain I saw another mountain, and on it were aloe trees, and those trees were full, like almond bark, and strong.

3When they take that fruit, it is better than any fragrance.

Notes

  • v1 "galbanum" — Greek chalbanē, a gum resin with a sharp smell. It is one of the four spices of the holy incense in Exodus 30:34, stacte and onycha and galbanum… and pure frankincense, the same Greek word in the Greek of Exodus. Sarara (Greek sarran) is not known from anywhere else.

  • v2 "aloe trees" — the Ge'ez. The Greek has no aloes: another mountain toward the east of the ends of the earth, and all the trees were full, and it puts the almonds in a phrase about rubbing. The Ge'ez wa-ṣənuʿ, and strong, has no match in the Greek.

  • v3 "when they take that fruit" — the Ge'ez. The Greek reads when they are rubbed; wherefore it was more fragrant than all spices: bark rubbed to release its smell, not fruit gathered. The Ge'ez yənaśśəʾəwwo, they take it, is the only point where the two part; both end on a fragrance better than every other.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 31
I saw another mountain with trees on it, and water flowed out, and from it came something like nectar, whose name is sarara and galbanum.
Beyond that mountain I saw another mountain, and on it were aloe trees, and those trees were full, like almond bark, and strong.
When they take that fruit, it is better than any fragrance.

chapters.title: The Tree of Wisdom
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 32

1After these fragrances, looking north over the mountains, I saw seven mountains full of choice nard and fragrant trees and pepper.

2From there I went over the summits of those mountains, far to the east, and I passed over the Red Sea and went far from it, and passed above the angel Zotiel.

The Garden of Righteousness

3I came into the garden of righteousness, and beyond those trees I saw many trees, great ones, growing there. Their fragrance was good, and they were great and good, and their beauty was abundant and glorious. There too was the tree of wisdom: those who eat from it learn great wisdom.

4It is like the carob tree, and its fruit is like a very beautiful cluster of grapes, and the fragrance of that tree spreads and reaches far.

5I said, "How beautiful this tree is, and how good and delightful to look at!"

6The holy angel Raphael, who was with me, answered me and said, "This is the tree of wisdom that your aged father and your ancient mother, who were before you, ate from. They learned wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden."

Notes

  • v2 "the Red Sea" — Ge'ez bāḥra ʾErtrā, Greek erythra thalassa, the Erythraean Sea: in Greek writers the name covers the Red Sea and the waters east of it. Enoch crosses it going east, toward the garden in Eden, in the east of Genesis 2:8. Zotiel is named only here: an angel in the Ge'ez, a bare name in the Greek.

  • v3 "the tree of wisdom" — the Greek first singles out two especially, very great, then the tree of wisdom, of whose fruit the holy ones eat. The Ge'ez has no holy ones: anyone who eats learns wisdom.

  • v4 "like the carob tree" — the Ge'ez. The Greek is twice as long here: like a fir in height, its leaves like the carob, its fruit like clusters of the vine. The Ge'ez keeps only the carob and the grapes. No witness calls it an apple, a fig or any tree named in Genesis.

  • v5 "How beautiful this tree is, and how good and delightful to look at" — Enoch's words are close to what Eve saw in Genesis 3:6, that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes. He stands where she stood and says what she saw.

  • v6 "your aged father and your ancient mother" — Adam and Eve, unnamed. The Ge'ez continues the story in the words of Genesis 3:7 and 3:23–24: their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out. The Greek breaks off after your father ate: the Greek manuscript of this part of the book ends here, and from 33 to 36 the Ge'ez is the only witness.

From there I went over the summits of those mountains, far to the east, and I passed over the Red Sea and went far from it, and passed above the angel Zotiel.
The Garden of Righteousness

I came into the garden of righteousness, and beyond those trees I saw many trees, great ones, growing there. Their fragrance was good, and they were great and good, and their beauty was abundant and glorious. There too was the tree of wisdom: those who eat from it learn great wisdom.
It is like the carob tree, and its fruit is like a very beautiful cluster of grapes, and the fragrance of that tree spreads and reaches far.
I said, "How beautiful this tree is, and how good and delightful to look at!"

The holy angel Raphael, who was with me, answered me and said, "This is the tree of wisdom that your aged father and your ancient mother, who were before you, ate from. They learned wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden."

chapters.title: The Gates of the Stars
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 33

1From there I went to the ends of the earth, and there I saw great beasts, each different from the other, and the birds too differed in their form and their beauty, and their voices differed one from another.

2East of these beasts I saw the ends of the earth, where heaven rests, and the gates of heaven were open.

3I saw how the stars of heaven come out, and I counted the gates they come out of, and wrote down all their exits, each one by its number, and their names in their order, their positions, their times and their months, as the angel Uriel who was with me showed me.

4He showed me everything and wrote it down for me. He also wrote down their names for me, and their laws and their tasks.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — from here to the end of chapter 36, 1 Enoch survives only in the Ge'ez. The Greek manuscript of these chapters stops at 32:6.

  • v2 "where heaven rests" — Ge'ez yāʿrəf, rests, lies down. The sky is pictured as a dome whose edge sits on the rim of the earth, as in 18:5, where Enoch saw at the edge of the earth the firmament of heaven above.

  • v3 "as the angel Uriel… showed me" — this is the subject of the book's next major part, the Book of the Luminaries (chapters 72–82), where Uriel shows Enoch the course of every light in the sky. Chapters 33 to 36 are a short preview of it.

  • v4 "He… wrote it down for me" — here the angel writes. Elsewhere Enoch is the scribe of righteousness (12:4, 15:1). In v3 Enoch writes; in v4 Uriel does. The Ge'ez keeps both.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 33

From there I went to the ends of the earth, and there I saw great beasts, each different from the other, and the birds too differed in their form and their beauty, and their voices differed one from another.
East of these beasts I saw the ends of the earth, where heaven rests, and the gates of heaven were open.

I saw how the stars of heaven come out, and I counted the gates they come out of, and wrote down all their exits, each one by its number, and their names in their order, their positions, their times and their months, as the angel Uriel who was with me showed me.
He showed me everything and wrote it down for me. He also wrote down their names for me, and their laws and their tasks.

chapters.title: The Winds of the North
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 34

1From there I went north, to the ends of the earth, and there at the ends of the whole earth I saw a great and glorious wonder.

2There I saw three gates of heaven open in the sky. Through each of them winds come out toward the north, and when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew and rain.

3From one gate the wind blows gently, but when it blows through the other two, it is with violence and hardship, and it comes on the earth, and they blow with violence.

Notes

  • v2 "three gates… winds come out" — the weather has doors. Job asks the same of the north: Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the storehouses of the hail? (Job 38:22). Enoch is shown them.

  • v2 "cold, hail, frost, snow, dew and rain" — six things, all from the north, and none of them described as punishment. The winds come out when they come out; the chapter is a survey, not a judgment.

  • v3 "when it blows through the other two" — the Ge'ez says with violence twice and runs its clauses together. The sense is clear, one gate gentle and two harsh, but the sentence is rough in the only witness that has it.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 34
From there I went north, to the ends of the earth, and there at the ends of the whole earth I saw a great and glorious wonder.
There I saw three gates of heaven open in the sky. Through each of them winds come out toward the north, and when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew and rain.
From one gate the wind blows gently, but when it blows through the other two, it is with violence and hardship, and it comes on the earth, and they blow with violence.

chapters.title: The Gates of the West
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 35

1From there I went west, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates open, just as I had seen in the east, the same number of gates and the same number of exits.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — one verse, and only in the Ge'ez. It completes the four-sided survey: east (33), north (34), west (35), south (36).

  • v1 "just as I had seen in the east" — the east gates of 33:2–3, where the stars come out. The west has the same number, and the stars that rise through one side set through the other (36:3).

  • v1 "the same number of exits" — Ge'ez muḍāʾāt, goings out, the word of 33:3, I wrote down all their exits. The numbers themselves are not given until chapters 72–82.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 35
From there I went west, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates open, just as I had seen in the east, the same number of gates and the same number of exits.

chapters.title: The Gates of the South and the Blessing
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 36

1From there I went south, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates of heaven open, and from there come the south wind, dew, rain and wind.

2From there I went east, to the ends of heaven, and there I saw three gates of heaven open toward the east, and above them small gates.

3Through each of these small gates pass the stars of heaven, and they go west on the path that was shown to them.

4When I saw it, I blessed, and I will always bless the Lord of glory, who has made great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to His angels and to the souls of men, so that they may praise His work and all His creation, so that they may see the work of His power and praise the great work of His hands, and bless Him forever.

Notes

  • v2 "small gates" — above the great gates of the east are smaller ones, one for the passage of stars. The great gates are for the sun and the winds; the book's own account of them is chapters 72–76.

  • v3 "on the path that was shown to them" — the stars do not choose their course; it is shown to them, the same verb Enoch uses of what Uriel showed him (33:3). The disobedient stars of 18:15 are punished precisely because they did not come out at their appointed times.

  • v4 "I will always bless the Lord of glory" — the title of 22:14 and 25:3. The chapter, and the whole first part of the book (chapters 1–36, the Book of the Watchers), ends on a blessing: the long journey through prisons, mountains, trees and gates closes with Enoch praising what he has been shown.

  • v4 "to His angels and to the souls of men" — the works are shown to both. The book began with angels who taught men what they should not know (8:1–3). It ends with God showing angels and men alike what He has made.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 36
From there I went south, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three gates of heaven open, and from there come the south wind, dew, rain and wind.
From there I went east, to the ends of heaven, and there I saw three gates of heaven open toward the east, and above them small gates.
Through each of these small gates pass the stars of heaven, and they go west on the path that was shown to them.

When I saw it, I blessed, and I will always bless the Lord of glory, who has made great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to His angels and to the souls of men, so that they may praise His work and all His creation, so that they may see the work of His power and praise the great work of His hands, and bless Him forever.

chapters.title: The Second Vision
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 37

1The vision he saw, the second vision of wisdom, which Enoch saw, the son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Kenan, son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam.

2This is the beginning of the words of wisdom that I took up to speak and to say to those who live on the dry land: Hear, you who were first, and see, you who come after, the holy words that I speak before the Lord of Spirits.

3It would be better to say these things to those who were first, but even from those who come after we will not hold back the beginning of wisdom.

4Until now such wisdom as I have received has not been given from before the Lord of Spirits: according to my insight, according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits, from whom the portion of eternal life has been given to me.

5Three parables came to me, and I speak them to those who live on the dry land.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — this opens the second part of the book, chapters 37–71, called the Parables from v5. From here to the end of chapter 71 the Ge'ez is the only witness: no Greek, Aramaic or Latin of these chapters survives.

  • v1 "son of Jared… son of Adam" — seven names, Adam to Enoch, the line of Genesis 5. Jude counts the same way when he quotes this book: Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Jude 14). Luke traces the same line upward to Adam, the son of God (Luke 3:37–38).

  • v2 "those who live on the dry land" — la-ʾəlla yaḫadru diba yabs. Yabs, dry land, is this part of the book's own word for the world of men. In the EOTC text it occurs 43 times in chapters 37–71 and not once in chapters 1–36, which say earth.

  • v2 "the Lord of Spirits" — ʾƎgziʾa Manāfəst, the name for God in the Parables, 106 times in chapters 37–71 of the EOTC text and never before this verse. Chapter 39:12 shows where it comes from.

  • v3 "It would be better to say these things to those who were first" — the sense is compressed: the words would have suited the generations of old, but they will not be kept from those who come after. The verse turns on qadamt, the first ones, and daḫāryān, the later ones, the same pair as v2.

  • v5 "Three parables" — məsālēyāt, parables, likenesses, figures. The book marks them itself: the first parable (38:1), the second parable (45:1), the third parable (58:1).

chapters.title: The First Parable
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 38

1The first parable. When the congregation of the righteous appears, and sinners are judged for their sins and driven from the face of the dry land,

2and when the Righteous One appears before the eyes of the righteous, whose chosen works hang on the Lord of Spirits, and light appears to the righteous and the chosen who live on the dry land — where then will the sinners live, and where will those rest who denied the Lord of Spirits? It would have been better for them if they had not been born.

3When the secrets of the righteous are revealed, the sinners will be judged, and the wicked will be driven from the presence of the righteous and the chosen.

4From then on those who hold the earth will no longer be mighty and exalted. They will not be able to look at the face of the holy, because the Lord of Spirits has made His light appear on the face of the holy, the righteous and the chosen.

5The kings and the mighty will perish at that time, and they will be given into the hand of the righteous and the holy.

6From then on no one will seek mercy for them from the Lord of glory, because their life has come to an end.

Notes

  • v1 "the congregation of the righteous… sinners are judged" — the parable opens with the two phrases of Psalm 1:5: the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous. The psalm says the sinners will not stand there; the parable describes the day it happens.

  • v2 "the Righteous One" — ṣādəq, singular: the first appearance of the figure at the center of the Parables, who will also be called the Chosen One (40:5) and the Son of Man (46:2). Stephen uses the same title in Acts: the prophets announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whom you betrayed (Acts 7:52).

  • v2 "whose chosen works hang on the Lord of Spirits" — sǝqul, hung, suspended. Their works depend on Him the way a thing hangs from a peg. The phrase comes back at 40:5 and 46:8.

  • v2 "It would have been better for them if they had not been born" — the same sentence Jesus says of the one who betrays the Son of Man: it would have been good for that man if he had not been born (Matthew 26:24).

  • v5 "The kings and the mighty" — the Parables name their enemy by rank: kings, the mighty, the exalted, those who hold the earth (v4). The word kings, nagaśt, occurs 20 times in chapters 37–71. In chapters 1–36 the judgment fell on the Watchers; here it falls on rulers.

  • v6 "from the Lord of glory" — the EOTC. Knibb's Ge'ez reads the Lord of Spirits. At 40:3 the two change places.

chapters.title: Under the Wings of the Lord of Spirits
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 39

1And it shall come to pass in those days that chosen and holy children will come down from the high heavens, and their seed will become one with the sons of men.

2In those days Enoch received books of zeal and wrath, and books of haste and turmoil. "There will be no mercy for them," says the Lord of Spirits.

3At that time a cloud and a whirlwind snatched me away from the face of the earth and set me down at the end of the heavens.

4There I saw another vision: the dwellings of the righteous and the resting places of the holy.

5There my eyes saw their dwellings with the angels and their resting places with the holy ones. They were asking and interceding and praying for the sons of men, and righteousness flowed before them like water, and mercy like dew on the earth. So it is among them forever and ever.

6In those days my eyes saw the place of the chosen, of righteousness and of faith. Righteousness will be in their days, and the righteous and the chosen will be without number before Him forever and ever.

7I saw their dwelling under the wings of the Lord of Spirits. All the righteous and the chosen before Him shine like the light of fire. Their mouths are full of blessing, and their lips praise the name of the Lord of Spirits. Righteousness before Him never fails, and uprightness before Him never fails.

8There I wanted to live, and my soul longed for that dwelling. My portion has been there from before, for so it has been established for me before the Lord of Spirits.

9In those days I praised and exalted the name of the Lord of Spirits with blessing and praise, because He has established me in blessing and praise, according to the good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits.

10For a long time my eyes looked at that place, and I blessed Him and praised Him, saying, "Blessed is He, and may He be blessed from before the world and forever.

11Before Him there is no end. He knows, before the world was created, what the world is, and what will be from generation to generation.

12Those who do not sleep bless You. They stand before Your glory and bless and praise and exalt, saying, 'Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits; He fills the earth with spirits.'"

13There my eyes saw all those who do not sleep. They stand before Him and bless and say, "Blessed are You, and blessed is the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever."

14My face was changed, because I could not look.

Notes

  • v1 "chosen and holy children will come down from the high heavens" — the words of the Watchers' story told again: at 6:2 the sons of heaven saw the daughters of men, and here children come down from the high heavens and their seed will become one with the sons of men. But these children are called chosen and holy, the words the Parables use for the righteous. The verse does not say whether it looks back to the fall of chapter 6 or forward to a holy descent, and the chapter goes straight on to Enoch.

  • v2 "Enoch received books" — the only verse in the chapter where Enoch is named in the third person, set between in those days and the Lord of Spirits' own words. The rest of the chapter is Enoch's I.

  • v5 "righteousness flowed before them like water" — the picture of Amos 5:24, let justice roll on like water, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream. In Amos it is a demand; here it is what the dwellers in heaven already have.

  • v6 "the place of the chosen, of righteousness and of faith" — both Ge'ez witnesses have the chosen, plural, and their dwelling in v7. Charles read the singular, the Elect One of righteousness and of faith, and moved parts of vv6–7 so that the Chosen One dwells under the wings. The Ge'ez as it stands keeps that figure for 40:5.

  • v7 "under the wings of the Lord of Spirits" — the shelter of Psalm 91:4: under His wings you will take refuge.

  • v12 "Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits; He fills the earth with spirits" — the song of the seraphim in Isaiah 6:3, Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory, with both halves changed: hosts becomes spirits, and glory becomes spirits. This is where the Parables' name for God comes from. The Lord of Spirits is the LORD of hosts, and the hosts are the spirits who fill heaven and earth.

  • v12 "Those who do not sleep" — the meaning of təguhān, Watchers, the wakeful ones of 1:5. These are the ones who stayed. In Revelation the four living creatures likewise have no rest day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy (Revelation 4:8).

  • v14 "My face was changed" — Daniel says the same after his vision of the Ancient of Days and the one like a son of man: my color changed on me (Daniel 7:28).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Four Presences
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 40

1After this I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, beyond number and reckoning, those who stand before the Lord of Spirits.

2I looked, and on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those who stand there. I learned their names, for the angel who came with me told me them and showed me all the hidden things.

3I heard the voices of those four presences as they sang praise before the Lord of Spirits.

4The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.

5The second voice I heard blessing the Chosen One and the chosen who hang on the Lord of Spirits.

6The third voice I heard asking and praying for those who live on the dry land, and interceding in the name of the Lord of Spirits.

7The fourth voice I heard driving away the satans and not allowing them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who live on the dry land.

8After this I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden, "Who are these four presences I have seen, whose voices I have heard and written down?"

9He said to me, "The first is the merciful and slow to anger, holy Michael. The second, who is over every sickness and every wound of the sons of men, is Raphael. The third, who is over every power, is holy Gabriel. The fourth, who is over repentance, for the hope of those who will inherit eternal life, is Phanuel."

10These are the four angels of the Lord Most High, and the four voices I heard in those days.

Notes

  • v1 "thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand" — the court of Daniel 7:10, where a thousand thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. Revelation counts the angels around the throne the same way (Revelation 5:11).

  • v2 "on the four sides… four presences" — gaṣṣ, face, the word behind presence. On the four sides is literally on His four wings, kənafihu, the word of 39:7, under the wings of the Lord of Spirits.

  • v3 "before the Lord of Spirits" — the EOTC. Knibb's Ge'ez reads the Lord of glory, the reverse of 38:6.

  • v5 "the Chosen One" — ḫəruy, singular: the first time the title appears. Older English versions say the Elect One. It is the word of Isaiah 42:1, My servant… My chosen one, in whom My soul delights. At the transfiguration the voice from the cloud says, This is My Son, the Chosen One; listen to Him (Luke 9:35).

  • v7 "driving away the satans… to accuse" — sayṭānāt, plural. Satan here is a job, not a single name: the accuser, as in Zechariah 3:1, where the satan stands at the high priest's right hand to accuse him. The fourth presence keeps the accusers away from the throne.

  • v9 "the merciful and slow to anger, holy Michael" — merciful and slow to anger are the words the LORD proclaims of Himself in Exodus 34:6. Here they describe the first of His angels.

  • v9 "Phanuel" — the same name as Penuel, face of God, the place where Jacob said, I have seen God face to face (Genesis 32:30). The four are presences, faces before God, and the fourth is named for it. At 9:1 the four were Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel; here Phanuel stands where Uriel stood.

speech.text: 1 Enoch 40
After this I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, beyond number and reckoning, those who stand before the Lord of Spirits.

I looked, and on the four sides of the Lord of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those who stand there. I learned their names, for the angel who came with me told me them and showed me all the hidden things.
I heard the voices of those four presences as they sang praise before the Lord of Spirits.
The first voice blesses the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.
The second voice I heard blessing the Chosen One and the chosen who hang on the Lord of Spirits.
The third voice I heard asking and praying for those who live on the dry land, and interceding in the name of the Lord of Spirits.
The fourth voice I heard driving away the satans and not allowing them to come before the Lord of Spirits to accuse those who live on the dry land.
After this I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden, "Who are these four presences I have seen, whose voices I have heard and written down?"

He said to me, "The first is the merciful and slow to anger, holy Michael. The second, who is over every sickness and every wound of the sons of men, is Raphael. The third, who is over every power, is holy Gabriel. The fourth, who is over repentance, for the hope of those who will inherit eternal life, is Phanuel."
These are the four angels of the Lord Most High, and the four voices I heard in those days.

chapters.title: The Secrets of Heaven
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 41

1After this I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the deeds of men are weighed in the balance.

2There I saw the dwellings of the holy and the dwelling of the chosen. My eyes saw there all the sinners who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits being driven out from there and dragged away. They could not stand, because of the punishment that goes out from the Lord of Spirits.

3There my eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and the thunder, and the secrets of the winds, how they are divided to blow on the earth, and the secrets of the clouds and the dew. There I saw the place they come out from, and from there they satisfy the dust of the earth.

4There I saw closed storehouses, from which the winds are divided, and the storehouse of the hail and the storehouse of the mist and of the clouds, and its cloud hovers over the earth from before the world.

5I saw the storehouses of the sun and the moon, where they go out and where they return, and their glorious return, and how one is more honored than the other, and their magnificent course. They do not leave their course; they neither add to it nor take from it, and they keep faith with each other by the oath they have sworn.

6The sun goes out first and travels its path at the command of the Lord of Spirits, and His name stands firm forever and ever.

7After this I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon. It completes its course in that place by day and by night, the one facing the other before the Lord of Spirits. They give thanks and praise and do not rest, for their thanksgiving is their rest.

8For the bright sun makes many turnings, for blessing and for curse, and the course of the moon's path is light for the righteous and darkness for sinners, in the name of the Lord of Spirits, who made a divide between the light and between the darkness, and divided the spirits of men, and strengthened the spirits of the righteous in the name of His righteousness.

9For no angel hinders, and no authority can hinder, because the Judge sees them all, and He judges them all before Him.

Notes

  • v1 "weighed in the balance" — the verdict written on Belshazzar's wall, you have been weighed in the balances (Daniel 5:27), here seen as the ordinary working of heaven: every human deed is weighed.

  • v2 "They could not stand" — the other half of Psalm 1:5, which the first parable began with (38:1): the wicked will not stand in the judgment.

  • vv3–4 the storehouses — the lightning, the winds, the hail, the mist and the clouds each have their store, as in Job 38:22, Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the storehouses of the hail? Enoch is shown what Job was asked about.

  • v5 "they keep faith with each other by the oath they have sworn" — the sun and moon hold their courses by an oath. The book tells the oath itself later, in 69:13–25, where heaven, earth, sea, sun and moon all are strong through it.

  • v7 "their thanksgiving is their rest" — the lights never stop, and their praise is what rest means for them.

  • v8 "a divide between the light and between the darkness" — māʾəkala bərhān wa-māʾəkala ṣəlmat, the construction of Genesis 1:4, where God made a division between the light and the darkness (Hebrew bein… u-vein). The same God who divided the light divides the spirits of men.

  • v9 "no authority can hinder, because the Judge sees them all" — the EOTC. Knibb's Ge'ez has only no angel hinders. Charles, working from other manuscripts, reads He appoints a judge for them all.

chapters.title: Wisdom Finds No Home
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 42

1Wisdom found no place where she could live, and her dwelling was in the heavens.

2Wisdom went out to live among the sons of men and found no dwelling. Wisdom went back to her place and took her seat among the angels.

3Iniquity went out of her storehouses. She found those she did not seek, and she lived among them like rain in the desert and like dew on thirsty ground.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — three verses on Wisdom and her opposite, set between Enoch's view of the heavenly lights (41) and the stars called by name (43). Both Ge'ez witnesses have it here.

  • vv1–2 "Wisdom… found no dwelling" — the reverse of Sirach 24, where Wisdom seeks a resting place among the nations and is told by her Creator, Make your dwelling in Jacob, and in Israel receive your inheritance (Sirach 24:7–8). In Sirach she finds a home on earth. Here she finds none and goes back to heaven. John's Gospel says it of the Word: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him (John 1:11).

  • v3 "like rain in the desert and like dew on thirsty ground" — the pictures of blessing, used for its opposite. At 39:5 righteousness flowed like water, and mercy like dew among the holy. Isaiah uses the same pictures for God's gift: I will pour water on the thirsty (Isaiah 44:3). Iniquity is welcomed the way rain is welcomed in a dry land.

  • v3 "She found those she did not seek" — Wisdom sought men and was refused; Iniquity did not need to seek, and was taken in.

chapters.title: The Stars by Name
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 43

1I saw other lightnings and the stars of heaven, and I saw how He calls them all by their names, and they listen to Him.

2I saw the balance of righteousness, how they are weighed by their light, by the breadth of their spaces and the day of their appearing, and their revolution: lightning begets lightning, and their revolution is by the number of their angels, and they keep faith among themselves.

3I asked the angel who went with me, who showed me what was hidden, "What are these?"

4He said to me, "The Lord of Spirits has shown you their likeness. These are the names of the righteous who live on the dry land and believe in the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever."

Notes

  • v1 "He calls them all by their names" — the words of Isaiah 40:26 about the stars: He brings out their host by number; He calls them all by name.

  • v2 "lightning begets lightning… by the number of their angels" — the verse is hard in both Ge'ez witnesses, and it is kept close to the words. The stars are weighed like deeds (41:1), each has an angel, and the lightning is born from them (44:1).

  • v4 "their likeness" — məsl, the word behind parable (37:5). The stars are a parable: each one is the name of a righteous person on earth. Daniel says the same of the wise: those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever (Daniel 12:3).

chapters.title: Lightning from the Stars
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 44

1Another thing I saw concerning the lightnings: how they rise from the stars and become lightning, and cannot leave them.

Notes

  • The whole chapter — one verse in both Ge'ez witnesses, finishing the thought of 43:2, lightning begets lightning.

  • "they rise from the stars and become lightning" — the flash is born from the star, the way the book has the stars born as names of the righteous (43:4).

  • "and cannot leave them" — the lightning stays bound to its star, as the sun and moon keep faith with each other (41:5) and the stars keep faith among themselves (43:2). Nothing in heaven breaks its bond.

chapters.title: The Second Parable
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 45

1This is the second parable, concerning those who deny the name of the dwelling of the holy ones and of the Lord of Spirits.

2They will not go up to heaven, and they will not come onto the earth. Such will be the portion of the sinners who deny the name of the Lord of Spirits, who are kept like this for the day of suffering and distress.

3On that day the Chosen One will sit on the throne of glory and will test their deeds, and their resting places will be without number. Their spirit will grow strong within them when they see My Chosen One, and those who call on My holy and glorious name.

4On that day I will make him dwell among them, and I will transform heaven and make it a blessing and a light forever.

5I will transform the dry land and make it a blessing, and I will make My chosen ones live on it. But those who commit sin and wrongdoing will not set foot on it.

6For I have seen My righteous ones and satisfied them with peace, and I have set them before Me. But My judgment of the sinners has drawn near to Me, so that I may destroy them from the face of the earth.

Notes

  • v1 "the second parable" — the second of the three announced at 37:5. The first began at 38:1; the third begins at 58:1.

  • v2 "They will not go up to heaven, and they will not come onto the earth" — the deniers belong nowhere: shut out of heaven, and with no part in the renewed dry land of v5.

  • v3 "the Chosen One will sit on the throne of glory" — the scene Jesus describes: when the Son of Man comes in His glory… He will sit on the throne of His glory (Matthew 25:31), and again in Matthew 19:28.

  • v3 "will test their deeds" — yaḫerri, from the same root as ḫəruy, the Chosen One. The Chosen One chooses: he sorts the deeds.

  • v3 "My Chosen One" — from here God speaks in the first person, with no words to introduce Him. The parable becomes His own speech.

  • v4 "I will make him dwell among them" — the EOTC has him; Knibb's Ge'ez names him, My Chosen One. Both mean the figure of v3.

  • vv4–5 "I will transform heaven… I will transform the dry land" — the promise of Isaiah 65:17, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The chosen live on the renewed land, as in Psalm 37:29, the righteous will inherit the land and dwell on it forever, and in the beatitude, the meek… will inherit the earth (Matthew 5:5).

chapters.title: The Head of Days and the Son of Man
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 46

1There I saw One who had a head of days, and His head was like white wool. With Him was another, whose face had the appearance of a man, and his face was full of grace, like one of the holy angels.

2I asked one of the holy angels who went with me and showed me all the hidden things about that Son of Man: "Who is he, and where is he from, and why does he go with the Head of Days?"

3He answered me and said, "This is the Son of Man who has righteousness, and righteousness lives with him. He will reveal all the treasures of what is hidden, because the Lord of Spirits has chosen him, and his portion has prevailed before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness forever.

4This Son of Man whom you have seen will rouse the kings and the mighty from their couches, and the strong from their thrones. He will loosen the reins of the strong and break the teeth of sinners.

5He will throw the kings down from their thrones and from their kingdoms, because they do not exalt him or praise him, or humbly acknowledge where their kingship was given them from.

6He will throw down the faces of the strong and fill them with shame. Darkness will be their dwelling, and worms will be their bed, and they will have no hope of rising from their beds, because they do not exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits.

7These are the ones who judge the stars of heaven and raise their hands against the Most High, and tread on the dry land and live on it. All their deeds show wrongdoing, and all their deeds are wrongdoing. Their power rests on their wealth, and their faith is in the gods they have made with their hands, and they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits.

8They drive the faithful out of His houses of assembly, those who hang on the name of the Lord of Spirits."

Notes

  • v1 "One who had a head of days, and His head was like white wool" — the Ancient of Days of Daniel 7:9, the hair of His head was like pure wool. Here He is described by His age, a head of days, and from v2 on it becomes His title. In Revelation the same white wool belongs to the one like a son of man: His head and His hair were white like wool (Revelation 1:13–14).

  • v1 "another, whose face had the appearance of a man" — Daniel 7:13: with the clouds of heaven came one like a son of man, and he came to the Ancient of Days. Daniel sees him come to the throne. Enoch sees him already beside it.

  • v2 "that Son of Man" — walda sabʾ, the first of the Ge'ez expressions the Parables use for this figure; the other main one, walda ʿəgwāla ʾəmmaḥəyāw, begins at 62:7. Daniel wrote like a son of man, a comparison. Here that Son of Man points at the one Enoch has just seen, and the rest of the Parables use it as his title. In the Gospels it is the name Jesus uses for himself.

  • v2 "the Head of Days" — the EOTC, Rəʾsa Mawāʿəl. Knibb's Ge'ez has the Ancient of Days, Bəluya Mawāʿəl, Daniel's own title.

  • v3 "He will reveal all the treasures of what is hidden" — Paul says of Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:3).

  • vv4–5 "throw the kings down from their thrones" — Mary's song: He has brought down the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the lowly (Luke 1:52). Break the teeth of sinners is Psalm 3:7, You break the teeth of the wicked.

  • vv6–7 "worms will be their bed… they judge the stars of heaven" — both from Isaiah 14, the taunt over the king of Babylon: maggots are spread beneath you, and worms are your covering (14:11), the king who said, I will raise my throne above the stars of God (14:13). The kings of the Parables are that king, many times over.

  • v8 "They drive the faithful out of His houses of assembly" — the EOTC, wa-yəsaddədu: the kings persecute the faithful. Knibb's Ge'ez has the passive, wa-yəssaddadu, they will be driven out of His houses: the kings' punishment rather than their crime. One letter's vowel separates the two.

chapters.title: The Blood of the Righteous
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 47

1In those days the prayer of the righteous and the blood of the righteous went up from the earth before the Lord of Spirits, and it was required.

2In those days the holy ones who live above the heavens will join together, and with one voice they will petition and pray and praise and give thanks and bless the name of the Lord of Spirits, because of the blood of the righteous that has been shed, so that the prayer of the righteous may not be set aside before the Lord of Spirits, so that judgment may be done for them, and their patience may not have to last forever.

3In those days I saw the Head of Days when He sat on the throne of His glory, and the books of the living were opened before Him, and all His host that is above the heavens and His council around Him stood before Him.

4The hearts of the holy were filled with joy, because the number of righteousness had arrived, and the prayer of the righteous had been heard, and the blood of the righteous had been required before the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • v1 "the blood of the righteous went up from the earth" — the voice of Abel's blood, crying out to Me from the ground (Genesis 4:10). In Revelation the souls under the altar cry out, How long, holy and true Master, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who live on the earth? (Revelation 6:10).

  • v1 "the blood of the righteous" — the Ge'ez here and in v4 is singular, ṣādəq, the same word as the Righteous One of 38:2. Both English renderings of the Ge'ez take it as the righteous in general, each one of them, and the plural prayer of the righteous beside it supports that. The singular is there for any reader who hears in it the Righteous One himself.

  • vv1, 4 "it was required" — tafaqda: the blood is demanded back, an account is called for. God says it of all shed blood after the flood: your blood… I will require (Genesis 9:5). The EOTC has the word in both verses; Knibb's Ge'ez only in v4.

  • v3 "the books of the living were opened" — the court of Daniel 7:10, the court sat, and the books were opened. The book of the living is Psalm 69:28, and in Revelation the books were opened, and another book was opened, which is the book of life (Revelation 20:12).

  • v4 "the number of righteousness had arrived" — the EOTC, baṣḥa ʾəlqʷā la-ṣədq. Knibb's Ge'ez has only it had arrived. The same answer is given to the souls under the altar in Revelation: they must rest a little longer, until their fellow servants and their brothers… were made complete (Revelation 6:11).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Knibb's Ge'ez and its English: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Name Before the Sun
chapters.html:
1 Enoch 48

1In that place I saw the fountain of righteousness, which never runs out, and around it were many fountains of wisdom. All the thirsty drank from it and were filled with wisdom, and their dwelling was with the righteous and the holy and the chosen.

2At that hour that Son of Man was named in the presence of the Lord of Spirits, and his name before the Head of Days.

3Before the sun and the signs were created, before the stars of heaven were made, his name was named before the Lord of Spirits.

4He will be a staff for the righteous and the holy, so that they may lean on him and not fall. He is the light of the nations, and he will be the hope of those whose hearts are grieved.

5All who live on the dry land will fall down and worship before him, and they will bless and praise and sing to the name of the Lord of Spirits.

6For this reason he was chosen and hidden before Him before the world was created.

7The wisdom of the Lord of Spirits has revealed him to the righteous and the chosen, for he has kept the portion of the righteous, because they have hated and rejected this world of wrongdoing, and hated all its works and its ways in the name of the Lord of Spirits. For in his name they are saved, and he has been the keeper of their life.

8In those days the kings of the earth, and the strong who hold the dry land, will be downcast in face because of the works of their hands, for on the day of their anguish and distress they will not save their souls.

9I will give them into the hands of My chosen ones. Like straw in the fire they will burn before the face of the righteous, and like lead in water they will sink before the face of the holy, and no trace of them will be found.

10On the day of their distress there will be fear on the earth. They will fall before him and not rise, and there will be no one to take them by the hand and raise them, because they have denied the Lord of Spirits and His Anointed. Blessed be the name of the Lord of Spirits.

Notes

  • v1 "In that place… drank from it" — the EOTC. Knibb's Ge'ez reads in those days, and has the thirsty drink from them, the fountains of wisdom. In the EOTC they drink from the fountain of righteousness itself.

  • v1 "All the thirsty drank" — Isaiah 55:1, Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters, and Revelation 21:6, To the thirsty I will give from the spring of the water of life. Wisdom, which found no home on earth (42:2), is here poured out for whoever is thirsty (49:1).

  • vv2–3 "his name was named… before the sun" — Psalm 72:17 says of the king: May his name endure forever; before the sun may his name flourish. The Parables make it a statement about time: the Son of Man was named before the sun was made. Peter says of Christ that he was foreknown before the foundation of the world, but revealed in the last times (1 Peter 1:20).

  • v4 "the light of the nations" — the servant's calling in Isaiah 49:6, I will make you a light of the nations, that My salvation may reach to the end of the earth. Simeon says it over the infant Jesus: a light for revelation to the Gentiles (Luke 2:32).

  • v5 "All who live on the dry land will fall down and worship before him" — Psalm 72:11, the same royal psalm as v3: all kings will bow down before him, all nations will serve him.

  • v6 "chosen and hidden before Him before the world was created" — the EOTC ends there. Knibb's Ge'ez adds and forever. The Son of Man is hidden: kept out of sight until the time to reveal him (v7).

  • v7 "he has been the keeper of their life" — the sense of the Ge'ez here is uncertain. The OCP's English of the Ge'ez gives he has become the guardian of their life; Charles gives according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.

  • v8 "the kings of the earth" — and in v10, the Lord of Spirits and His Anointed. Both phrases are from Psalm 2:2: the kings of the earth set themselves… against the LORD and against His anointed. The kings of the Parables are the kings of the psalm.

  • v9 "like lead in water they will sink" — the Song of the Sea: they sank like lead in the mighty waters (Exodus 15:10). The kings go down as Pharaoh's army did.

  • v10 "there will be fear on the earth" — the EOTC, fərhat. Knibb's Ge'ez reads ʿəraft, rest: on the day of their distress there will be rest on the earth. One witness has the earth afraid, the other at rest once the kings are gone.

  • v10 "His Anointed" — masiḥu, His Messiah: the first time the title appears in the book. It comes once more, at 52:4.
